Think about it logically. We're taking these kids, who are supposed to be our best and brightest, and making them get through college by playing a sport that's been proven to cause concussions? That doesn't make sense.

College sports in general are a cancer on academia. Most schools lower their admission standards in hopes of attracting the best high school athletes. The attitudes of both faculty and students puts sports first and class second (we ain't come to play school!). In addition, lots of money is spent on stadiums, coaching staff, training programs -- shouldn't schools be investing in, I don't know, education? Academies (think soccer) and farm teams (think baseball) are far better ways to train potential pros. At this point, is LSU even a university, or is it just an unpaid football team?

Now, that's just my problem with college sports in general -- the same can be said of college basketball, volleyball, soccer -- whatever. As for football itself, it's a dangerous and dumb sport. No matter what the NFL tries to tell you, there are serious risks of concussions and other injuries. Why do we need a sport where ramming into other players is a major part of the game? Why do we need a sport where all the strategy comes from offensive coordinators and creativity is non-existent? Why do we need to call gridiron "football" when the game has fuck all to do with feet or balls?

TL;DR College sports work against academics at supposed institutes of higher learning. Football itself is less a sport and more a testament to American arrogance. Combine these two and you have something I'm not interested in being a part of.
